import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import pearsonr

# Exclude EC6 (1958) aggregate row, only member countries
areas = [30528, 674843, 248717, 301336, 2586, 41526]
gdps = [58.316, 312.966, 400.554, 265.192, 2.938, 83.351]

corr, _ = pearsonr(areas, gdps)
# Round to two decimals
corr_rounded = round(corr, 2)

# Determine correlation relation
if corr_rounded >= 0.7:
    relation = "Strong positive correlation"
elif 0.3 <= corr_rounded < 0.7:
    relation = "Weak positive correlation"
elif -0.3 < corr_rounded < 0.3:
    relation = "No correlation"
elif -0.7 < corr_rounded <= -0.3:
    relation = "Weak negative correlation"
else: # <= -0.7
    relation = "Strong negative correlation"

print(f"Final Answer: {relation}, {corr_rounded}")
